The pacing of the story feels very balanced and appropriate for its quiet, atmospheric tone. The actual "story time" only spans a few minutes as Johanna enters the house, walks into the kitchen, and goes down the cellar stairs. By slightly "stretching" these brief moments through rich sensory details (the creak of the door, the taste of the rusty water, the fermenting smell), the writer builds a quiet suspense and highlights the emotional weight of the setting. Simultaneously, the writer uses extreme "compression" by summarizing the protagonist's entire absence in a single two-word sentence ("Zwanzig Jahre" / "Twenty years"), which effectively contrasts the long passage of time with the immediacy of her physical return.
